Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED check breaks organization slug assignment

Line 151 changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` in an unrelated file. Previously, `slug` was set directly only when billing was disabled, and stored as `metadata.requestedSlug` when billing was enabled until payment completed. true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-Google calendar services always use the first host's destinationCalendar instead of matching the credential

In a collective booking, `event.destinationCalendar` contains the destination calendars of all hosts, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` calls `createEvent` once per host credential with the full `event`. Unlike `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` (which looks up the entry matching `credentialId`), `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128 and 164), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156) all take `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`. When a secondary host uses Office 365, Lark, or CalDAV/Apple Calendar, their service will use the first host's `externalId` (e.g., a Google Calendar address), causing Office 365 and Lark API calls to fail with 404/invalid calendar ID and causing `BaseCalendarService` to filter out all calendars and silently skip creating the event.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments target the same defect in non-Google calendar implementations (Office365/Lark/Base): they do not accept/use credentialId to select the matching host destination calendar, so they fall back to the first entry and break collective bookings. The candidate describes the runtime consequence of the contract mismatch the golden flags.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await deletions and bypasses `try/catch`

Converting the `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` callback to `async` in `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` (line 125), `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` (line 125), and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (line 553) causes `.forEach` to ignore the returned promises. As a result, `Reschedule` / `requestReschedule` no longer waits for `getCalendar` and `calendar.deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` to finish before completing, and any rejection inside the `async` callback escapes the surrounding `try / catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught and logged. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe async callbacks inside forEach not being awaited, causing fire-and-forget deletions, unhandled rejections, and try/catch bypass; the candidate proposes the same Promise.all/map fix.

false_positives.candidate:
All app modules are still eagerly imported at module load time

Each property in `appStore` is assigned the result of calling `import("./...")` directly (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). Because these expressions are evaluated when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is loaded, importing `@calcom/app-store` immediately triggers dynamic imports for all 28 apps in parallel rather than loading only the requested app on demand. To defer loading until an app is accessed, each property should be a getter (e.g. `get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar"); }`) or a thunk (`() => import("./applecalendar")`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
